title: Police raid on the Spikes brothers' Dreamland Cafe in Los Angeles
summary: Police order Reb Spikes to stop Black men dancing with white women; he refuses and the club is raided and closed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Um, what about, uh, the raids out in California that you told me about? Thanks. Mm-hmm.

We were playing at, uh, at the Dreamland Cafe, nightclub, you know. Mm-hmm. We were playing for the Spike Brothers. You heard of them. Mm-hmm. We were playing for the Spike Brothers. Ori and I at 4th and Stanford in Los Angeles. I'll never forget that. And, uh, we were playing there one night, one Sunday night, I'll never forget it. And the police had told, Reb Spikes was the tenor player, you see. Yeah, Reb Spikes, Reb and Johnny. Johnny was the oldest brother. Reb was a tall, nice-looking boy. And he had told Reb to cut the colored men from dancing with the white women, you see. Cut it out. Mm-hmm. Let them dance with their race, you know. Couldn't stop them from coming into place, but they didn't want them dancing together, you see.

Well, Reb was a fiery fellow, you know, see. So he told them that he wasn't going to do it, because there was no law against it, you see. There was no discrimination, and he wasn't going to stop it, you see. So the police said, all right, we're going to stop it, we're going to close you up. Well, he didn't believe it, I don't guess. He couldn't see the right people. So that next Sunday night, he come back down there. Three police come back there. Two colored police and a white blue. Detectives. So he called them off the bandstand. He said, Reb, did I tell you I didn't want this mixed stance under this place? Well, one word brought on another, he stopped the band, he said, well, we're going to raid your place tonight. And when he said that, well, him and Reb got heated arguments, you see. And they handcuffed him and like to beat him to death. It was pitiful when they beat him. Put handcuffs on him, beat him, so he was a boy, and closed up the place. All that throwed us out of the job. But when we first went there, we were playing at Cadillac for a guy named Lee Larkins. That's the guy that sent for us, Lee Larkins. On Central Avenue between 5th and 6th.
And what kind of place was the cabaret? Cabaret. I clubbed his lap, just like Lee's.
